html:
The Numu, or Northern Paiute, are a people of the western Great Basin, a wide dry country of mountain ranges and lake basins in Nevada, eastern Oregon, northeast California and southwest Idaho. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, related to Shoshone and Ute.

Bands were named after a main food: the cui-ui fish eaters of Pyramid Lake, the cattail eaters, the pine nut eaters. Families moved with the seasons to fish, hunt rabbits and pronghorn, and gather seeds. The Pyramid Lake War of 1860, after miners rushed in for the Comstock Lode, cost them land and water.

The writer Sarah Winnemucca, a Northern Paiute, published one of the first books by a Native American woman in 1883. The prophet Wovoka, who began the Ghost Dance in 1889, was a Northern Paiute from Nevada. See also Northern Paiute and Yahooskin.
